the two-nucleon correlations are sensitive to the nuclear symmetry energy but not to other nuclear matter properties.

the two-nucleon correlations in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies are sensitive to nuclear symmetry energy and can thus be used to extract information about the density dependence of symmetry energy.
isospin effects in the two-nucleon correlations are sensitive to nuclear symmetry energy and the sensitivity is enhanced with decreasing incident energy and increasing impact parameter.

the isospin dependence of nuclear equation of state and its effects on the dynamics of heavy ion collisions at the intermediate energies.
the effects of nuclear symmetry potential on the emission time and relative emission sequence of protons and neutrons.

the two-nucleon correlations are sensitive to the nuclear symmetry energy and the isospin dependence of the nucleon-nucleus potential, but not sensitive to the incompressible of nuclear matter and the isospine dependence of the nucleonnucleon scattering cross sections.
the two-nucleon correlations are sensitive to the nuclear symmetry energy, and the isospin effects can be used to extract information of the symmetry energy at high densities.

the nucleon-nucleus correlation function in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies could be a useful probe for nuclear symmetry energy at high densities.

the two-nucleon correlations are sensitive to nuclear symmetry energy and could be used to probe the density dependence of the symmetry energy at high densities.
